record.paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.original_question: For the five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies detected by Fermi-LAT, whose apparent isotropic luminosities in the 0.1–100 GeV band are about 10^44–10^47 erg s−1 and therefore blazar-like, are the high gamma-ray luminosities mainly produced because the relativistic jet is viewed at a small angle and has a high beaming factor?

evidence.quote: So far five radio-loud NLSy1 galaxies have been detected at high significance by Fermi-LAT: 1H 0323+342, SBS 0846+513, PMN J0948+0022, PKS 1502+036, and PKS 2004−447.

Their average apparent isotropic luminosity in the 0.1–100 GeV energy band is between 10^44 erg s−1 and 10^47 erg s−1, a range of values typical of blazars. This could be an indication of a small viewing angle with respect to the jet axis and thus a high beaming factor for the γ-ray emission, similarly to blazars.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies that have been detected at high significance in the high-energy gamma-ray band (0.1–100 GeV) by space-based gamma-ray telescopes: 1H 0323+342, SBS 0846+513, PMN J0948+0022, PKS 1502+036, and PKS 2004−447. Their measured apparent isotropic gamma-ray luminosities in the 0.1–100 GeV band lie in the range 10^44–10^47 erg s^−1, comparable to those of blazars (radio-loud active galactic nuclei whose relativistic jets point close to the observer's line of sight, so that the observed flux is strongly enhanced by relativistic Doppler beaming with a beaming factor δ = [Γ(1 − β cos θ)]^−1, where Γ is the bulk Lorentz factor of the jet, β = v/c, and θ is the angle between the jet axis and the line of sight).

Determine whether the high observed gamma-ray luminosities of these five NLSy1 galaxies are predominantly the consequence of viewing a relativistic jet at a small angle θ with respect to the jet axis, yielding a large Doppler beaming factor δ for the gamma-ray emission, in analogy with blazars.
artifact.category_tag: Relativistic jets in active galactic nuclei
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent multi-wavelength studies (VLBI/MOJAVE kinematics, SED modeling, variability) provide strong evidence that the gamma-ray-emitting radio-loud NLSy1s host relativistic jets viewed at small angles with high bulk Lorentz factors and large Doppler beaming factors, analogous to blazars. However, exact viewing angles and beaming factors for each individual source still carry uncertainty, so the picture is broadly confirmed but not fully quantitatively settled.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic Jets in Gamma-Ray-Emitting Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: These sources, similarly to blazars, are thought to possess relativistic radio jets inclined at small angle to the line of sight.
status_evidence.claim: Gamma-ray NLSy1s are inferred to have jets at small viewing angles, supporting the beaming hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Properties of flat-spectrum radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Updated MOJAVE kinematics on six of these sources indicates high bulk Lorentz factors and small viewing angles in three cases.
status_evidence.claim: VLBI kinematics confirm high Lorentz factors and small angles for several gamma-NLSy1s.

status_evidence.title: General Physical Properties of Gamma-Ray-emitting Narrow-line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Luminosity, variability and spectral properties of the NLSy1 in γ-rays indicate a blazar-like behaviour, suggesting a relatively small viewing angle and high beaming factor.
status_evidence.claim: SED and variability analyses confirm blazar-like beaming for the gamma-ray NLSy1 sample.
